vedic_reference.note: The name Tej is derived from the Sanskrit word 'तेजस्' (tejas), which means 'shine, splendor, brilliance, or radiance'. In Hindu mythology, Tej is also the name of the god Agni, who is the god of fire and the guardian of the sacrificial fire. The name is also associated with the god Indra, who is the king of the gods and the god of rain, thunder, and lightning.

Ultimately, living a virtuous life can be equated with having a high Tejas, bringing peace, wisdom, and prosperity into one's life.

historical_references.reference: Tej was a legendary king of the Solar Dynasty in Hindu mythology, also known as the Ikshvaku Dynasty. He is said to have ruled during the early Treta Yuga, a golden age in Hindu mythology. Tej is most famous for his generous hospitality towards the sage Vishwamitra, who was performing a great sacrifice. Vishwamitra was so pleased with Tej's hospitality that he granted him the boon of having a son who would be a great king and a destroys of demons. This son was later known as Rama.
